clue.text: Plant in it is in a comfortable situation

definitions.meaning: a low-growing meadow plant with trefoil leaves, a shamrock-type herb

definitions.text: in it is in a comfortable situation
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'in ...' means living in ease and comfort, so being in this plant is being comfortably off

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the trefoil meadow herb; the other comes from the idiom for living in luxury, where grazing cattle feed well.

clue.text: Picked third-rate footwear

parts.note: C is the grade for third class, after A and B
hose are stockings or socks, worn on the feet

explanation.surface: Someone selected cheap, shoddy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third-rate' looks like an adjective for the footwear, but it gives C, the third grade after A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked and selected are synonyms, both past tense of making a choice.

clue.text: Finished with a cricket score having gone on too long

parts.note: over means ended or done with
a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket match ended with a score after play lasted beyond its scheduled time.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed an allotted time is to overstay the schedule; 'having gone on too long' is the past participle sense.

clue.text: Attendants have broken out to make cross outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the angering word wraps around the shuffled letters

parts.note: to enrage someone is to make them angry

indicators.note: broken signals that the word out is smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Attendants have escaped and are making some angry person furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as an adjective or a crucifix, but 'to make cross' is a verb phrase meaning to anger; 'broken' shuffles OUT and 'outside' wraps the angering verb round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of followers or retinue accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Way to university-or mental dullness?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
in British usage one goes up to university, so UP means at or towards college

explanation.surface: A route to college, or perhaps a state of mental fog for the student?
explanation.walkthrough: Going 'up' to university is a British idiom, so UP stands for 'to university'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state where the mind barely functions, a torpor of the senses.

clue.text: During the course of it he irritated men associated with them

indicators.note: during the course of signals the letters run continuously inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In the middle of something, a man annoyed the people linked to some group.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed without its letter count (5). The run straddles 'it he irritated', which gives the possessive pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun marks things belonging to or connected with a group of people.

clue.text: Old king just heard a surprised exclamation

indicators.note: heard means the word for just is taken as spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: just means fair, as in a fair judge
oh is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch has only just let out a startled cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only', but it means FAIR, said aloud as PHAR because of 'heard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of ancient Egypt were titled thus, monarchs of the old kingdoms along the Nile.

clue.text: The odd athlete who supplies contraband booze?

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or odd
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: A strange sportsman doubles as a smuggler of illicit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as 'odd' is dated British slang ('a rum do'); the surface makes you think of rum the drink, which fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of alcohol, especially during Prohibition, was known by this name.

clue.text: Telling the truth sharpens the edges of tragedy

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it on a stone

indicators.note: the edges of a word here are its first and last letters, taken from tragedy

explanation.surface: Truthfulness hones a tragedy to its sharpest form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the edges of tragedy' means its first and last letters, not a pair at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Truthfulness and candour are the quality of speaking without deceit.

clue.text: Old Russian force ready at sea to surround marines

indicators.note: to surround says the jumbled letters go around the marines' abbreviation
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of ready are jumbled

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A Soviet-era navy, prepared on the ocean, encircles a marine detachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like part of the naval picture but signals the jumble of 'ready'; 'to surround' wraps those letters round the marines, split after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union's army bore this name from 1918, a military force of the former USSR.

clue.text: Original keel not in ship's essential structural frameworks

indicators.note: in tells us the shuffled letters sit inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: original means novel or newly made, so keel and not are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ship's original keel is missing from the vessel's basic framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' is an unusual anagram signal: it means freshly made, so 'keel' and 'not' are remade; 'in' puts them between the two letters of the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony frames of animals, and figuratively the bare supporting outlines of any structure.

clue.text: Fabric produced by prophet, the fool!

parts.note: a seer foresees the future
a sucker is a gullible person, easily fooled

explanation.surface: Some cloth made by a soothsayer, the idiot!
explanation.definitionFit: A light puckered cotton cloth, often striped, used for summer suits.

clue.text: Approximately nothing lost making border

indicators.note: lost tells us something goes missing from the word for approximately

parts.note: about means roughly or approximately
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Losing almost nothing creates a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes O (nothing) from ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to adjoin or touch along an edge, as neighbouring plots of land do.

clue.text: Beast from the east also seen in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: seen in places the word for also inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: An animal from Asia has also been spotted in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white bear is native to China, so it comes from the east.

clue.text: Dance music cut up-is one a special arrangement?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for cut is read upwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches

indicators.note: a special arrangement means is one a are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Dance music has been chopped up: is it a special musical arrangement?
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOP into POL in this down light, and 'special arrangement' rearranges IS ONE A into ONAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Polish processional dance in triple time, and the music written for it, as by Chopin.

clue.text: Extended help with writing style

parts.note: long means extended in length
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: Prolonged assistance with one's penmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary handwriting with words written out in full, as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Authors appear in most of new catalogues

indicators.note: most of means the word for new loses its final letter

parts.note: novel means new or original
lists are catalogues of items

explanation.surface: Writers show up in the bulk of the latest publishers' catalogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of NOVEL, leaving NOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of fiction books are authors of a particular kind.

clue.text: I'll deal with abuse

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to treat something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Someone promises to tackle mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal with' is TREAT, as in treating a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat or handle cruelly; the verb sense of abuse.

clue.text: More drunk if the grit flies about

indicators.note: flies about suggests letters scattering, so the grit is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets more tipsy if sand blows around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, so the comparative means more inebriated.

clue.text: Big shot about to back malicious person

parts.note: VIP is a very important person, a big shot

indicators.note: to back means the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An important person is about to support a spiteful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to back' reads like 'ready to support', but RE (about) is reversed to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, and by extension a treacherous or spiteful individual.

clue.text: North Country river follows old grazing area

indicators.note: follows means the river comes after the word for old

parts.note: past means old or former
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, in northern England

explanation.surface: A northern English river flows past an ancient meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire; 'North Country' is a British name for northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland where livestock feed is a pasture, a meadow for grazing.

clue.text: Poles have silver problem

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Polish people have trouble with their silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but gives the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hitch or unexpected difficulty.

clue.text: Crooned with girls appearing in protective spectacles

parts.note: crooned means sang softly, so sung
lasses are girls, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A singer performed while young women wore eye protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted glasses that shield the eyes from bright light.

clue.text: Femme fatale wrong to conceal note

indicators.note: to conceal means the word for wrong hides the note inside it

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A seductress is wrong to hide a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message but is the musical note RE.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, sea nymphs lured sailors to their doom; hence a dangerously alluring woman.

clue.text: Wader, for instance, starts to remove every twig

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A wading bird starts stripping every twig from a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of remove, every and twig.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron-type bird that wades in shallow water to feed.

clue.text: Bird is very cold sitting on top of nest

indicators.note: sitting on means the cold word is placed before the letter that follows

parts.note: bitter weather is extremely cold

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of nest

explanation.surface: A bird sits frozen on top of its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of nest' gives N, which 'sitting on' puts after BITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A booming marsh bird of the heron family.

clue.text: Cardinal points to several sheets of paper showing title

parts.note: E and S are east and south, two of the cardinal compass points
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A cardinal's notes on a few pages reveal his honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but cardinal points are compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesy title written after a man's name in formal British correspondence.

clue.text: Go wrong with mission

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and means with or along with

explanation.surface: A mission goes awry.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip to do a task, such as shopping, is an errand.

clue.text: When given a quick kiss, expressed a view

indicators.note: expressed means spoken aloud, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: as means when, and pecked means given a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Someone stated an opinion while receiving a peck on the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: AS PECKED (when given a quick kiss), spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook or perspective; one facet of a situation as seen from a viewpoint.
